newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower on lack of fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower on lack of fund buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed lower as early buying fizzled out amidst weak market sentiment and lack of support from foreign funds, dealers and analysts said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended down 6.70 points at 1,181.07, after hitting an early high of 1,190.27. It fell to a low of 1,175.35 in intraday trading.

"There's not enough money in the market at the moment to sustain a rebound. In fact, some of the funds are looking for opportunity to sell," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage house. "The market looks to be heading for 1,150."
Added an institutional dealer at a local brokerage: "I am afraid that margin calls may affect this market. The market has fallen below support at 1,800 and sentiment is weak."
But some dealers said the market was slightly oversold in recent days and some technical bounce can be expected.
At the close, market volume stood at 335 million shares. Losers overwhelmed gainers 612 to 79.

Aokam Perdana again led volume, with the stock falling another 56 cents to 4.08 ringgit. The company on Tuesday reported a net loss of 46.47 million ringgit for the six months ended December 31, 1996, against a 6.35 million loss previously.
